title: Adaptive physical pool size with logical Givens views
hypothesis: A smaller physical expert pool plus paid layer-role coordinates reaches the target quality of a four-expert independent bank with lower complete bytes, while simple pool tying does not.
physical_object: K physical 8x8 experts selected from a four-function Givens orbit
mirror_coordinate: one per-role Givens angle relative to an assigned physical expert center
logical_multiplicity: four logical routed functions from K in {1,2,4} physical experts
controls: standard global pool at K=1,2,4 without Views

development.selection_metric: heldout operator nRMSE, actual serialized bytes and router+expert MAC proxy

fresh.reason: synthetic orbit exactly matches native direct-angle control; no fresh claim pursued

storage.authority: actual compressed NPZ inference payload bytes

success_gate: At least one K<4 view condition has heldout nRMSE <=0.02 and >=25% fewer complete bytes than the independent K=4 bank; compare compute and native direct-angle controls.
failure_gate: FAIL for Mirror-specific value if direct-angle Givens matches the same payload/function, or if savings/quality do not meet the gate.
boundaries: Designed one-plane orthogonal orbit only; no trained MoE, learned routers, language model, or natural task-bank claim.
Pool centers and assignments are fixed from the declared angle grid; no fresh task tuning.
The experiment measures operator reconstruction; active expert routing is a fixed paid role-index table.
